question.problem:
The heights, in centimeters, of six randomly selected tulips drawn from a population were measured. The results are shown below.

$$
35,\,37,\,42,\,51,\,48,\,51
$$

Calculate the value of the statistic ${\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\frac{({X}_{i}-44)^{2}}{n-1}$ for this particular sample.
question.worked_solution:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sequence of random variables representing a random sample of size $n$ drawn from a population. A statistic is a random variable expressed as a function of ${X}_{i}.$

Statistics cannot involve unknown population parameters.

Note the following notation:

- ${X}_{i}$ denotes the random variable representing the $i$th observation in a random sample, and

- ${x}_{i}$ is the value of ${X}_{i}$ in a specific sample.

For the given sample, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{6}\frac{({x}_{i}-44)^{2}}{6-1} & =\frac{1}{5}((35-44)^{2}+(37-44)^{2}+(42-44)^{2}+(51-44)^{2}+(48-44)^{2}+(51-44)^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(81+49+4+49+16+49) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(248) \\  & =49.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of our statistic for this particular sample is $49.6\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.$
